title: Group Policy
summary: Policy processing failures on domain-joined PCs.

events.title: Group Policy could not get the list of policies
events.meaning: Windows could not ask the domain for the list of Group Policy objects.
events.causes: A network or DNS problem, or no access to a domain controller.
events.next: Check the network, DNS and that a domain controller can be reached, then run a policy update.

events.title: Group Policy could not find the user or computer name
events.meaning: Windows could not work out the user or computer name when processing policy.
events.causes: A network or name lookup problem.
events.next: Check the network connection and DNS, then run a policy update.

events.title: Group Policy could not find the computer name
events.meaning: Group Policy processing failed because Windows could not resolve a name.
events.causes: A DNS or network problem with the domain controller.
events.next: Check DNS settings and the connection to the domain controller.

events.title: Group Policy could not read a policy file
events.meaning: Windows could not read a policy file from the domain's shared policy folder.
events.causes: A network, permissions or replication problem with the policy folder.
events.next: Check that the policy folder can be opened from this PC and that the domain controllers replicate correctly.

events.title: A Group Policy setting could not be applied
events.meaning: Windows failed to apply one group of policy settings. The message names which.
events.causes: A problem in that setting area or its local settings.
events.next: Read the extension named in the message and check that area.

events.title: Group Policy could not apply registry settings
events.meaning: Windows could not apply the registry-based settings of a policy object.
events.causes: A damaged policy file or a permissions problem.
events.next: Check the policy object named in the message, and its permissions.

events.title: Group Policy failed because of a network problem
events.meaning: Policy processing failed because the PC could not reach a domain controller.
events.causes: The network was not ready at start-up, a VPN was not connected, or a firewall blocks it.
events.next: Check network and VPN connectivity at start-up, then run a policy update.
